role: Low-level, hardware-agnostic Rust interface over NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Qualcomm, Intel, Google, and AWS accelerators plus Vulkan/D3D12/OpenGL/WebGPU. Agent-first: predictable shapes, terse APIs, errors that name the failing operation. Includes a faster drop-in replacement for cudarc.

ontology.api: ironaccelerator_core::ontology::operations() -- every trait-surface operation with its effects: allocates, executes, compiles, transfers, blocks, unchecked

capabilities.name: allocation.as_ptr
capabilities.description:
Raw device pointer. Backends that virtualise pointers return a \
 handle cast to a raw pointer, so it is not always dereferenceable \
 on the host. Declares: unchecked.

note: requires_grant and budgeted are now DERIVED from the effects the crate declares per operation. An earlier version of this file said both were judgement, which was true before the ontology module existed. The effect set is deliberately not a read_only boolean. On a device the authority to use it and the cost of using it are the same resource, so the operations that allocate, execute, compile or transfer are both granted and budgeted together -- an alignment that would look like a mistake elsewhere in this stack and is correct here. compute.pipeline is granted for a distinct reason and declares `compiles` rather than `executes`: it turns caller-supplied bytes into device instructions without running them. A caller gating only on execution would let arbitrary program text reach the device unexamined, and a test pins the two apart. allocation.as_ptr is the one operation granted without consuming anything. It hands out a raw pointer -- which backends that virtualise pointers return as a handle, not a dereferenceable host address -- and it is the only member of the `unchecked` set. A test asserts that set stays exactly one entry, because this crate trades guard-rails for throughput by design and each further trade should be reviewed as one. Unlike the CLI tools in this stack, this ontology is hand-maintained: Rust offers no reflection over trait methods, so no drift test can walk the real surface the way clap allows. Adding a trait method without declaring it here will not fail a build. The module says so in its own preamble rather than implying a guarantee it cannot make.
